title: KDDI and Telehouse spends £220 million to expand London Docklands campus
snippet: Purchase of Inventory Estate paves the way for a new high-density, AI-ready data centre The post KDDI and Telehouse spends £220 million to expand London Docklands campus appeared first on Total Telecom.
fullText:
Press Release

Purchase of Inventory Estate paves the way for a new high-density, AI-ready data centre

KDDI Corporation and Telehouse International Corporation of Europe Limited have completed the purchase of the Inventory Estate in East India Dock, London from LaSalle Investment Management and Trilogy Real Estate for more than £220 million (US$294 million).

The land acquisition will support a new high-density, AI-ready data centre as part of the expansion of Telehouse’s existing London Docklands campus, the most connected data centre campus in Europe.

The site’s proximity to the campus offers the opportunity to add capacity at scale, capitalise on the well-established connectivity ecosystem operating at the campus, and meet future customer demand amid increasing constraints on land and power.

The planned development will offer high-performance digital infrastructure including high-density colocation services, low-latency connectivity, and AI-led workloads. 65 MVA of power has been secured for the site, providing a foundation for phased, long-term expansion.

The purchase reinforces Telehouse’s long-term commitment to investing in the UK’s digital infrastructure and the continued growth of the country’s digital economy. It follows the announcement of Telehouse West Two, a nine-storey data centre building currently in development at the Telehouse London Docklands campus, which is due for completion in 2028.

As plans for this latest development progress, Telehouse will continue its longstanding, proactive engagement with local stakeholders and the wider Tower Hamlets community, with a focus on sustainable development, local investment, and employment opportunities.

Mark Pestridge, Managing Director, Telehouse Europe, says: “The purchase of the Inventory Estate represents an important step in the long-term development of our London Docklands campus, one of Europe’s leading connectivity hubs. It provides space for future expansion to support our customers’ digital growth ambitions, including the crucial innovation that is taking place across industries such as healthcare, education, and financial services. As demand for AI-ready infrastructure grows, we remain focused on sustainable operations, community engagement, and creating opportunities in the local area.”

Takayo Takamuro, Executive Officer, European Chief Executive, Board Director, Telehouse, says, “This acquisition supports the next phase of our growth and our commitment to supporting customers’ AI ambitions. The new data centre will be one of the largest facilities in the Telehouse London Docklands campus, reinforcing its role as the leading connectivity hub in Europe.”

Chris Lewis, Head of UK Transactions, LaSalle Investment Management, added: “The extensive refurbishment works undertaken in partnership with Trilogy Real Estate to regenerate East India Dock into a world-class mixed-use innovation campus have paved the way for this next exciting development on the Inventory Estate. We look forward to watching its progress as the Docklands are set to host an important AI-ready data centre, critical to powering London’s tech sector.”

title: Beyond the Cable: Ookla analyst talks M&As and the tapestry of telecom
snippet: Mike Dano, a lead industry analyst at Ookla, has identified more than half a dozen ISPs that could be M&A targets. We talked to him about what’s behind the trend. The post Beyond the Cable: Ookla analyst talks M&As and the tapestry of telecom appeared first on Total Telecom.
fullText:
Podcasts

Mike Dano, a lead industry analyst at Ookla, has identified more than half a dozen ISPs that could be M&A targets. We talked to him about what’s behind the trend.

By Brad Randall, Broadband Communities

Recent analysis from Ookla’s Mike Dano has identified a handful of ISPs that stand out from the pack as targets for potential acquisition.

Speaking to Beyond the Cable, Dano said a combination of factors is driving M&A in 2026, including political factors.

The list includes names you’d expect: Allo Fiber, Gateway Fiber, LiveOak Fiber, Wire 3, Ripple Fiber, Intrepid Fiber, and Ezee Fiber.

While the M&A trend in telecom is undeniable, with AI and BEAD also playing major roles, Dano says he’s most interested in how the convergence is going to play out.

He said fiber is one element of the tapestry of telecom.

“We’ve got satellite players that are making an increasing impact in the industry, we’ve have fixed wireless that is obviously gobbling up a lot of net broadband customers in recent years,” he said.

Dano said he wants to know if the combination of a mobile and fixed service plays a key role in coming years, and how that eventually impacts fiber providers.

“Once you roll up these fiber networks, then what?” he asked.

Watch the full interview with Dano on Spotify or listen to it on Apple Podcasts in full.

Dano’s full analysis on the subject is available in a September 28 post titled “Assessing the ‘Land Grab’ in the U.S. Fiber Market: Who’s Next?” on Ookla’s website.

title: Israel’s Discover-Tech suspected of using ads to track Starlink users
snippet: The company is accused of purchasing ads with the purpose of geolocating and surveilling users The post Israel’s Discover-Tech suspected of using ads to track Starlink users appeared first on Total Telecom.
fullText:
News

The company is accused of purchasing ads with the purpose of geolocating and surveilling users

A report from Reuters claims that Israeli ad tech firm Discover-Tech has been targeting Starlink users for surveillance, according to six anonymous sources familiar with the matter.

The sources claim that the company pursued a large scale ad purchasing campaign aimed at surreptitiously gaining access to targeted users’ location and tracking their internet activity.

The report builds upon a previous report published on 15 October by TrendAI, a subsidiary of Japanese security firm Trend Micro, which first revealed suspicious ad purchasing activity by a company referred to by a codename, “Shadow-Earth-79”.

Shadow-Earth-79, since revealed to be Discover-Tech, was shown to be the number one bidder for ad-space via Starlink in over 100 countries, including Syria, Libya, Yemen, and South Sudan – countries with “almost no demand” for Western advertisements.

In total, Discover Tech accounted for 12.9% of winning advertisements in Starlink traffic, almost five-times higher than the average of 2.6%.

Online advertisers typically compete for ad space on websites and apps through a complex auction process. During this process, data about the end receivers of those ads can be shared with bidders. This data, when recorded over time and combined with other available information, can allow for individual identification, geolocation, and targeting with surveillance software.

TrendAI’s report said that the company’s bidding patterns showed an “obvious skew” towards Starlink users, likely related to “targeting and tracking infrastructure rather than a commercial advertising operation.”

The same day that TrendAI’s report was released, Discover-Tech was also accused of wider surveillance efforts by cybersecurity watchdog Citizen Lab and ad tech specialist Confiant.  This included using Candiru spyware alongside its ads to compromise user devices, including 5 Windows devices at the Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera between 2024 and 2025.

“Very likely hundreds of millions of people would have been touched by Discover-Tech,” explained Confiant cofounder Jerome Dangu.

Alphabet (Google), IAB Europe, and Comcast’s Beeswax have all cut the company off from their ad platforms in the past month.

title: Deutsche Telekom tests automated vehicle logistics with Volkswagen
snippet: The insights gained provide a foundation for further developing automated logistics solutions The post Deutsche Telekom tests automated vehicle logistics with Volkswagen appeared first on Total Telecom.
fullText:
Press Release

The insights gained provide a foundation for further developing automated logistics solutions

How can vehicles be moved automatically across logistics sites and safely integrated into existing processes? Over the past two years, Volkswagen, Deutsche Telekom, Finnish technology company Unikie, and the Bremen Institute for Production and Logistics at the University of Bremen (BIBA) have explored this question at the Port of Emden. The federally funded innovation project “AutoLog,” supported by the Federal Ministry of Transport (BMV), aimed to examine the potential of automated vehicle movements for more efficient, future-ready port logistics.

The test site is located on a logistics area close to the Port of Emden. In addition to parking areas and roadways, it includes a heavily used traffic circle. Under these conditions, the project partners were able to examine different traffic situations. A particular focus was on the interaction between automated and manually controlled vehicles during ongoing logistics operations, as well as on integrating the technology into existing processes.

Christian Vollmer, member of the Volkswagen Brand Board of Management for Production and Logistics and also a member of the extended Group Executive Committee: “AutoLog shows the potential automated driving offers for our logistics. For us, it is important not only to develop new technologies under laboratory conditions, but also to test their practical suitability where our logistics operations take place every day. Together with our partners, we have gained important insights in Emden into how vehicle movements can be automated more intelligently in the future and how logistics processes can continue to evolve. We want to use these experiences to further develop the technology.”

Technology components work together

From a technical perspective, AutoLog combines several components into an integrated system for automated vehicle logistics. The Unikie Marshalling Solution (UMS) provides overarching control and coordination of the vehicles. This requires vehicle technology, environmental sensing, communications infrastructure, and logistics software to work together reliably.

A digital representation of the parking areas supports the planning and coordination of vehicle movements. For communication between the system and the vehicles, the project uses Deutsche Telekom’s public 5G network, which has been enhanced with additional functions to meet the application’s requirements. The UMS runs on an edge cloud system. The data is processed close to the mobile network through a high-speed fixed-line fiber-optic connection, creating the technical conditions needed for time-critical applications.

Klaus Werner, Managing Director, Business Customers, Telekom Deutschland: “AutoLog shows how industrial-grade connectivity can serve as the digital backbone for automated processes across vehicle logistics. The interplay of low-latency, reliable connectivity, edge infrastructure, and intelligent vehicle control creates the technical foundation for scaling automated vehicle distribution from the end of the production line via rail and ship to the end customer.”

Insights for advancing vehicle logistics

Other project priorities included standardized communication and safe interaction between people and technology. AutoLog follows the ISO 23374 standard for Automated Valet Parking and explores how automated vehicles can be integrated into complex logistics environments. This includes interaction with people and other road users, as well as coordinating automated vehicle movements with existing logistics processes.

Vesa Kiviranta, CBO Automotive & Marshalling Solutions at Unikie: “In Emden, we demonstrated that automated vehicle movements can be tested even in a demanding logistics environment with mixed traffic. The interaction between our marshalling solution, the existing infrastructure, and manually driven vehicles is an important step. The insights gained help us further develop the technology and assess its market readiness for use in other logistics environments.”

Elsewhere in the Volkswagen Group, work is also underway to automate vehicle movements. As part of a collaboration between the AutoLog project and the Audi site in Ingolstadt, the project partners tested the automated loading of vehicles onto railcars. This puts another step in the vehicle logistics process in focus: precisely positioning vehicles as they are transferred to rail transport. The successful pilot adds another use case to the experience gained in Emden and shows how automated driving can reshape and further develop a range of tasks along the logistics chain.

With the conclusion of AutoLog, the joint pilot phase comes to an end. The insights gained are intended to inform the further development of automated logistics processes and provide a basis for evaluating additional potential applications. Over the long term, automated vehicle movements could help make logistics operations more flexible, safer, and more sustainable, while opening up new opportunities for organizing vehicle transportation at plant and terminal sites.
